content: The chair of the working group on operational updates and priorities is Virginia MacDonald, representing the World Health Organization (WHO) in Switzerland. The group includes members such as Monica Alonso Gonzalez from the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) in the USA, Maria Au from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) in the USA, and Jesus Garcia Calleja, a consultant for the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria (GFATM) in Switzerland. Other members include Martin Choo from the Asia Pacific Council of AIDS Service Organizations in Malaysia, Fatou Maria Drame from Enda Santé in Senegal, Avi Hakim from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in the USA, and Suman Jain, Margaret Kugonza, and Sandra Kuzmanovska, all representing GFATM in Switzerland. Additional members include Linh-Vi Le from the WHO Western Pacific Regional Office (WPRO) in the Philippines, Riku Lehtovuori from the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime in Austria, Virginia Loo, a WHO consultant in the USA, Neema Makyao from the Ministry of Health in Tanzania, Bradley Mathers, a WHO consultant in Switzerland, Keith Sabin from UNAIDS in Switzerland, Olga Varetska from the Alliance for Public Health in Ukraine, Annette Verster from WHO in Switzerland, and Jinkou Zhao from GFATM in Switzerland. The working group on adolescent girls and young women is chaired by Shona Dalal from WHO in Switzerland. Members include Lize Aloo from GFATM in Switzerland, Rachel Baggaley from WHO in Switzerland, Haddi Cham from CDC in the USA, Ines Dourado from the Federal University of Bahia in Brazil, Regina Guthold from WHO in Switzerland, Anita Hettema from the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI) in Eswatini, Elizabeth Irungu from Partners PrEP in Kenya, Aleya Khalifa from UNICEF in the USA, Ruth Laibon from UNAIDS in Switzerland, Annalise Limb from USAID in the USA, Irene Mukui from the Ministry of Health in Kenya, Saiqa Mullick from the Wits Reproductive Health and HIV Institute in South Africa, Ombeni Mwerinde from Unitaid in Switzerland, Van Thi Thuy Nguyen from WHO in Vietnam, Reshmie Ramautarsing from the Thai Red Cross in Thailand, Jason Reed from Jhpiego in the USA, Janet Saul from the Office of the Global AIDS Coordinator (OGAC) in the USA, and Chandramouli Venkataraman from WHO in Switzerland. The working group on voluntary medical male circumcision is co-chaired by Julia Samuelson from WHO in Switzerland and Lycias Zembe from UNAIDS in Switzerland. Members include Esther Mary Aceng-Dokotum from WHO in Ethiopia, Wole Ameyan from WHO in Switzerland, Mary Nana Brantuo from WHO in Namibia, Alicia Carbonell from WHO in Mozambique, Maria Carrasco from USAID in the USA, Lastone Chitembo from WHO in Zambia, Bhavin Jani from WHO in Tanzania, Mugagga Kaggwa from WHO in Uganda, Valerian Kiggundu from USAID in the USA, Christine Kisia from WHO in Kenya, Nomthandazo Lukhele from the Ministry of Health in Eswatini, Simbarashe Mabaya from WHO in Zimbabwe, Tebogo Madidimalo from WHO in Botswana, Busisiwe Msimanga-Radebe from WHO in South Africa, Zebedee Mwandi from Jhpiego in the USA, Ishmael Nyasulu from WHO in Malawi, Harilala Nirina Razakasoa from WHO’s African Regional Office (AFRO) in Congo, Jules Mugabo Semahore from WHO in Rwanda, Maaya Sundaram from the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF) in the USA, Susan Tembo from WHO in Lesotho, and Anne Thomas from the Department of Defense in the USA. The advisors for hepatitis, infection safety, and blood safety include Philippa Easterbrook, Yvan Hutin, and Junping Yu, all from WHO in Switzerland. Editorial consultant services were provided by Ward Rinehart and Sarah Johnson from Jura Editorial Services, who performed technical editing. Financial support for this work was provided by the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the United States President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria, and the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation. WHO also acknowledges the contributions of institutions that provided staff time and other in-kind support for the development of these guidelines. The document includes a glossary of terms and abbreviations relevant to the health sector response to the HIV epidemic. It emphasizes the importance of collecting, analyzing, and using data at all levels, from patient care to global monitoring, to ensure an effective response to the epidemic. The guidelines aim to strengthen program management by identifying and addressing gaps in service access, coverage, and quality across the HIV service cascade, from prevention to viral suppression. The audience for these guidelines includes HIV program staff and their partners involved in strategic information collection and analysis at all levels of the health sector.
